title: Cap. IV Arg. 7: τρόπος of mercy and justice is the one true predestination — Rom. 9:22
latin: Arg. 7. Τρόπος secundum quem Dominus Deus in aliis ostendit suam misericordiam, in aliis justitiam, est vera et unica praedestinatio; Atqui decretum salvandi credentes ex una, condemnandi incredulos ex altera parte, est talis τρόπος: Ergo hoc decretum est vera et unica praedestinatio. Dicunt Majorem ab ipsis Contraremonstrantibus admitti: Minorem probari ex Rom. ix. 22. ubi per vasa misericordiae et irae intelliguntur credentes et increduli.
pass_a: Argument 7. The manner according to which the Lord God shows his mercy in some, his justice in others, is the true and only predestination; But the decree of saving believers on the one side, of condemning unbelievers on the other, is such a manner: Therefore this decree is the true and only predestination. They say the Major is admitted by the Contraremonstrants themselves: the Minor is proved from Rom. 9:22, where by vessels of mercy and of wrath believers and unbelievers are understood.
pass_b: Arg. 7. The τρόπος by which the Lord shows his mercy in some and his justice in others is the true and only predestination. But the decree to save believers on one side and condemn unbelievers on the other is such a τρόπος. Therefore that decree is the true and only predestination. They say Contraremonstrants admit the Major; the Minor they prove from Rom. 9:22, where vessels of mercy and of wrath mean believers and unbelievers.

lemmas.gloss: manner of showing mercy and justice

title: Cap. IV Arg. 7 Sol: double praeordinatio — intention and execution both declare mercy and justice
latin: Sol. In mente Divina concipere oportet quoad Electos praeordinationem duplicem: unam, quae ordinem intentionis continet; alteram, quae ordinem exsecutionis: Utraque autem inservit declarandae misericordiae et justitiae Divinae. Exempli causa; Quod Deus ante jacta mundi fundamenta decreverit Jacobum et Petrum diligere, ac eorundem in donatione gratiae specialis ac vitae aeternae misereri; Esavum autem et Judam in hac designatione ad infallibilem vitae gratiaeque consecutionem praeterire, atque in peccatis suis obfirmatos justae condemnationi deputare: in hisce, inquam, decretis continetur abyssus quaedam misericordiae et justitiae, cujus penetrandae nulla acies humani ingenii sufficit. Jam vero quod idem Deus in verbo suo patefecerit, se decrevisse omnes credentes salvare, omnes incredulos damnare, quodque (in die judicii) cum ad exsecutionem ventum fuerit, de facto Esavum et Judam damnet, Jacobum et Petrum servet: exprimit etiam misericordiae justitiaeque Divinae egregium ac singulare specimen.
pass_a: Solution. In the Divine mind one ought to conceive a double praeordination as to the Elect: one, which contains the order of intention; the other, which contains the order of execution: But both serve for declaring the Divine mercy and justice. For example; That God before the foundations of the world were laid decreed to love Jacob and Peter, and to have mercy on the same in the donation of special grace and eternal life; but to pass by Esau and Judas in this designation to the infallible attainment of life and grace, and to appoint those hardened in their sins to just condemnation: in these decrees, I say, there is contained a certain abyss of mercy and justice, for penetrating which no sharpness of human genius suffices. But now that the same God in his word has opened that he has decreed to save all believers, to damn all unbelievers, and that (on the day of judgment) when it has come to execution, in fact he damns Esau and Judas, saves Jacob and Peter: he also expresses an excellent and singular specimen of the Divine mercy and justice.
pass_b: Sol. In God's mind regarding the elect, conceive a double praeordination: one of intention, one of execution — both serve to declare divine mercy and justice. Example: before the world's foundations God decreed to love Jacob and Peter and have mercy on them in special grace and eternal life; to pass by Esau and Judas for that infallible attainment of life and grace, and appoint those hardened in their sins to just condemnation — an abyss of mercy and justice no human wit can pierce. And that the same God has opened in his word that he decreed to save all believers and damn all unbelievers, and that on judgment day he in fact damns Esau and Judas and saves Jacob and Peter — that too is a singular specimen of divine mercy and justice.

lemmas.lemma: Jacobum et Petrum / Esavum et Judam
lemmas.gloss: Jacob and Peter vs Esau and Judas

title: Cap. IV Arg. 7 Sol: do not bind whole praedestinatio to the execution τρόπος — Major not universal
latin: Cum igitur in utraque praeordinatione elucescat misericordia ac justitia Divina; hoc est, tam in ea qua Deus decrevit singulares quasdam personas facere credentes, quam in ea altera qua eisdem credentibus vitam aeternam promittit et praestat; tam in ea qua decrevit quarundam personarum non misereri eousque ut easdem emolliat, fidemque illis inspiret; quam in ea qua eosdem obduratos et incredulos damnat: non debuerunt adversarii ad posteriorem τρόπον alligare totam et integram praedestinationis rationem; quae propriissime versatur in priori. Hisce praelibatis, dico Majorem syllogismi propositi non esse universalem. Nam omnis τρόπος in quo apparet erga alios misericordia, erga alios justitia Dei, non est illa unica praedestinatio cujus inscrutabilem profunditatem Scripturae tantopere celebrant; quamvis in ipsa praedestinatione proprie sumpta, qua alii ad vitam mediante gratia speciali destinantur, alii in morte mediante proprio demerito relinquuntur, misericordia ac justitia illustrissime agant partes suas.
pass_a: Since therefore in both praeordinations the Divine mercy and justice shine forth; that is, both in that by which God decreed to make certain singular persons believers, and in that other by which he promises and performs eternal life to the same believers; both in that by which he decreed not to have mercy on certain persons so far as to soften the same and inspire faith in them; and in that by which he damns the same hardened and unbelieving: the adversaries ought not to have bound the whole and entire reason of predestination to the latter manner; which most properly turns upon the former. These things having been tasted beforehand, I say that the Major of the proposed syllogism is not universal. For every manner in which mercy toward some, justice of God toward others appears, is not that only predestination whose inscrutable depth the Scriptures so greatly celebrate; although in predestination itself properly taken, by which some are destined to life by means of special grace, others are left in death by means of their own demerit, mercy and justice most illustriously play their parts.
pass_b: So in both praeordinations mercy and justice shine — in the decree to make certain persons believers, and in the decree that promises and gives those believers eternal life; in the decree not to have mercy so far as to soften some and inspire faith, and in the decree that damns the same hardened unbelievers. Adversaries should not bind the whole reason of predestination to the latter τρόπος; it turns most properly on the former. With that premised: the Major is not universal. Not every τρόπος in which mercy toward some and justice toward others appears is that unique predestination whose depth Scripture so celebrates — though in predestination properly taken, by which some are destined to life by special grace and others left in death by their own demerit, mercy and justice play their parts most clearly.

lemmas.gloss: do not bind whole to latter manner

title: Cap. IV Arg. 7 Sol: Minor — Ego salvabo credentes shows equal mercy/justice; discrimination from acts
latin: Accedo ad Minorem, in qua affirmatur, decretum salvandi credentes, et condemnandi incredulos, esse illam praeordinationem secundum quam Deus erga alios declarat misericordiam suam, erga alios justitiam suam. Fatemur juxta hoc decretum spectari et declarari in eventu misericordiam Dei erga alios, et erga alios justitiam: verum longe altiori modo exserit se misericordia in praedestinationis decreto, et justitia in decreto praeteritionis. Decretum hoc, Ego salvabo credentes, Ego condemnabo incredulos, in se consideratum omnibus ex aequo ostendit et facit misericordiam, omnibus ex aequo ostendit et facit justitiam: Nihil promittit aut exhibet Jacobo et Petro, quod non sub iisdem conditionibus promittit et exhibet Esavo et Judae; nihil negat Esavo aut Judae quod non sub iisdem conditionibus negat Jacobo et Petro. Nam quod Jacobus et Petrus participes fiant misericordiae et vitae aeternae, Esavus et Judas non fiant, id discriminis non fluxit ex decretorum diversitate quoad ipsas personas, sed ex personarum diversitate in suis operationibus.
pass_a: I come to the Minor, in which it is affirmed that the decree of saving believers, and of condemning unbelievers, is that praeordination according to which God declares his mercy toward some, his justice toward others. We confess that according to this decree the mercy of God toward some, and justice toward others, is looked upon and declared in the event: but in a far higher manner mercy puts itself forth in the decree of predestination, and justice in the decree of passing by. This decree, I will save believers, I will condemn unbelievers, considered in itself shows and makes mercy equally to all, shows and makes justice equally to all: It promises or exhibits nothing to Jacob and Peter which it does not under the same conditions promise and exhibit to Esau and Judas; it denies nothing to Esau or Judas which it does not under the same conditions deny to Jacob and Peter. For that Jacob and Peter become partakers of mercy and eternal life, Esau and Judas do not, that discrimination did not flow from diversity of decrees as to the persons themselves, but from diversity of the persons in their operations.
pass_b: Now the Minor: that the decree to save believers and condemn unbelievers is the praeordination by which God declares mercy toward some and justice toward others. We grant that on that decree mercy and justice are seen and declared in the event — but mercy puts itself forth far higher in the predestination decree, and justice in the decree of passing by. I will save believers, I will condemn unbelievers, taken in itself, shows and makes mercy equally to all, justice equally to all. It promises Jacob and Peter nothing it does not under the same conditions promise Esau and Judas; it denies Esau or Judas nothing it does not under the same conditions deny Jacob and Peter. That Jacob and Peter share mercy and eternal life while Esau and Judas do not comes not from diverse decrees about the persons, but from the persons' diversity in their operations.

lemmas.gloss: I will save believers — equal to all

title: Cap. IV Arg. 7 Sol close: proper praedestinatio decrees special mercy to elect, denial to others
latin: Illa autem misericordia quae in decreto praedestinationis se exserit, decernit, praeparat, donat singulari alicui praedestinatae personae quod alii non praedestinatae minime decernit, praeparat aut donat. Illa etiam Justitia quae in decreto reprobationis consideratur, decernit aliquid negandum reprobato quod idem decernitur haud negandum Praedestinato. Non igitur sufficit ad constituendum praedestinationis proprie dictae decretum, quod secundum illud intervenientibus diversis humani arbitrii actibus, misericordia in hos, justitia in illos exseratur; sed requiritur tale decretum quod ex primaria intentione et speciali operatione Dei decernentis, includat misericordiam hisce exhibendam; et ex liberrima et justissima Dei voluntate innuat eandem specialem misericordiam aliis denegandam.
pass_a: But that mercy which puts itself forth in the decree of predestination decrees, prepares, gifts to some singular predestinated person what to another not predestinated it least decrees, prepares, or gifts. That Justice also which is considered in the decree of reprobation decrees something to be denied to the reprobate which the same is decreed by no means to be denied to the Predestinated. It does not therefore suffice for constituting the decree of predestination properly so called, that according to it, with diverse acts of human choice intervening, mercy is put forth upon these, justice upon those; but such a decree is required which from the primary intention and special operation of God decreeing includes the mercy to be shown to these; and from the most free and most just will of God hints that the same special mercy is to be denied to others.
pass_b: But the mercy that puts itself forth in the predestination decree decrees, prepares, and gifts to a singular predestinated person what it does not decree, prepare, or gift to one not predestinated. The justice in the reprobation decree decrees something denied to the reprobate that is not denied to the Predestinated. So it is not enough for predestination properly so called that, with diverse acts of human choice intervening, mercy falls on these and justice on those. What is required is a decree that, from God's primary intention and special operation in decreeing, includes mercy to be shown to these, and from his freest, most just will hints that the same special mercy is to be denied to others.
